Order 
This miscellaneous second appeal under Section 71(6) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been filed against order dated 23/07/2024 passed by Third District Judge, Morena, District Morena/Appellate Tribunal in MCA No.115/2022 as well as order dated 11/04/2022 passed by Adjudicating Authority/Additional District Magistrate, Morena in Case No.36/20/Food Safety.

2. Facts necessary for disposal of present appeal, in short, are that on 28/08/2019 at about 06:30 PM, Food Safety Officer alongwith his team visited the house of appellant No.1- Aekesh Tyagi because they had received an information that appellant No.1 Aekesh Tyagi and his uncle Vrindawan Tyagi- appellant No.2 are engaged in the business of adulterated milk.
The police party was also accompanied by other officers and police.
It was informed by police officer that both the appellants have run away from the spot.

One can of 20 litres containing hydrogen peroxide, two opened tins containing 15 litres of refined oil, four blue- coloured empty milk cans were found kept at the door of the house of appellant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4050 2 MSA-15-2024 No.1, whereas three tins of refined palm oil, which were in sealed condition, were found hidden in wheat husk.

The house of appellant No.2 is situated near to the house of appellant No.1, and behind the house of appellant No.2 one stove was constructed over which the utensil was kept, six tins of refined palm oil, which were kept in a hidden condition in the bushes, were seized.

sentences.text: 1 An information was also received that appellant No.1 had also hidden certain articles in the field of Ram Ratan Tyagi and, accordingly, 13 tins of refined palm oil were seized from the field of Ram Ratan situated on the backside of his house, whereas 10 tins of refined palm oil were seized from the field of Ram Ratan which was situated in front of his house.
In all, 32 tins of refined oil of the same batch number and manufactured by the same company were seized.
Sampling was done, and the seized articles were sent to the Food Analyst.
The refined palm oil was found to be an adulterant under Section 3 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
Accordingly, notices were issued to appellants and other persons.
Since the appellants and other noticees did not pray for re-testing of seized articles, therefore, a complaint was filed.
3. The appellants as well as other noticees filed their written statement.
The evidence of Anil Pratap Singh Parihar, the Food Safety Officer was recorded.
The evidence of appellant No.1, Deen Dayal Tyagi and Anil Tyagi were also recorded.

Thereafter, the Adjudicating Authority found that appellants are guilty of violating the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011, and accordingly, appellants and other persons were hold guilty of violating Sections 57 and 58 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Rule 26(2)(ii)(v) of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011.

Accordingly, for violating Section 57 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, a penalty of Rs.2,00,000/- and for violating Section 58 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4050 3 MSA-15-2024 2006, a penalty of Rs.2,00,000/- in all a total penalty of Rs.4,00,000/- on appellant No.1, and similarly, the similar penalties were also imposed on appellant No.2 as well as other noticees namely, Deen Dayal Tyagi and Banti Tyagi.

sentences.text: 4. Appellants as well as Deen Dayal Tyagi and Banti Tyagi filed their appeal under Section 70 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

The Appellate Tribunal by the impugned order has exonerated Deen Dayal Tyagi and Banti Tyagi, whereas has dismissed the appeal filed by appellants and imposed a penalty of Rs.20,000/- each for violating Sections 57 and 58 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

5. Challenging the order passed by Appellate Tribunal, it is submitted by counsel for appellants that there is nothing on record to suggest that seized articles were seized from the places which were in possession of appellants.

Even the Food Safety Officer has accepted that certain more articles are required for manufacturing adulterated milk, but the same were not recovered, therefore, it is clear that appellants were not engaged in manufacturing adulterated milk and invited the attention of this Court towards cross-examination of Anil Pratap Singh Parihar to the effect that "generally the persons who are engaged in manufacturing synthetic milk use refined oil, Maltose Moulder,
skimmed milk powder, RM chemical and liquid detergent", and it was admitted that "Maltose Moulder, skimmed milk powder, RM chemical and liquid detergent were not found from the spot".
6.
Considered the submissions made by counsel for appellants.
7. It is the case of the prosecution that at the time of search, appellants had ran away from their house.

Appellants had filed their reply to the complaint and in that reply, it was categorically admitted that the Food Safety Team had visited the house of appellant No.1 and at that time,

sentences.text: appellants were not present in their NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4050 4 MSA-15-2024 house.
Why the appellants ran away from the spot has not been clarified.

Merely by saying that appellants were not in their house at the time of inspection, is not sufficient to meet out the allegations that appellants after noticing the search party had run away from the house because appellants have not explained or disclosed their location at the time of search.
Thus, it is clear that immediately after noticing the search party, appellants ran away from the spot, indicating their guilty mind.

There is no reason to disbelieve that 32 tins were seized either from the house of appellant No.1 or from the place immediately behind the house of appellant No.2, as well as from the fields of Ram Ratan.
All the palm oil tins were of the same batch and were manufactured by the same company.
This cannot be a coincidence, unless and until all the 32 tins of palm oil are purchased in one go.

Palm oil, which was manufactured by the same company and were of same batch, was also seized from the door of the house of appellant No.1 as well as from a place behind the house of appellant No.2, and field of Ram Ratan.
8. Under these circumstances, it is clear that appellants were manufacturing synthetic milk.
9. So far as the non-recovery of Maltose Moulder, skimmed milk etc. is concerned, it cannot be said that a synthetic milk cannot be manufactured without using the aforesaid articles.
Non-recovery of skimmed milk powder and Maltose Moulder also indicates that the milk which was being manufactured by appellants was completely synthetic.

10. Be that whatever it may be.
11.

Since appellants have not clarified the purpose for which they had kept seized articles in such a large quantity and appellants have not clarified why a stove and utensils were found just behind the house of appellant No.2, this Court NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4050 5 MSA-15-2024 is of considered opinion that the prosecution has successfully proved that appellants were engaged in manufacturing synthetic milk.

12. So far as the question of penalty is concerned, Appellate Tribunal has already taken an undue sympathetic view in favour of appellants and has reduced the penalty from Rs.2,00,000/- to Rs.20,000/- for violating Sections 57 and 58 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, therefore,
no further interference is required.
13. Accordingly, no case is made out warranting interference.

The order dated 23/07/2024 passed by Third District Judge, Morena, District Morena/Appellate Tribunal in MCA No.115/2022 as well as order dated 11/04/2022 passed by Adjudicating Authority/Additional District Magistrate,
Morena in Case No.36/20/Food Safety are hereby affirmed.
14. The appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

(G. S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE PjS/-
